However, the largest natural lake in South America is **Lake Titicaca**, which is located on the border between Peru and Bolivia. It is the highest navigable lake in the world, sitting at an elevation of about 3,812 meters (12,507 feet) above sea level. While it is not the largest by surface area—Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela is larger—it is the most prominent and significant lake in South America in terms of altitude and cultural importance.

So, the largest natural lake in South America is **Lake Titicaca**.
